tools.name: document_open
tools.description: Open an existing document in the editor panel. Use this when the user asks to see or pull up a document that exists but isn't currently visible in the editor — for example after switching devices, refreshing, or when the editor panel was closed.

surface_id.description: The ID of the document to open

tools.name: document_create
tools.description: Create a new long-form document in a rich text editor that opens in workspace mode with chat docked to the side. Use this for ANY document or written piece the user asks you to write, draft, compose, or prepare — a letter (cover/business/formal/reference/support/application letter), memo, proposal, report, brief, essay, article, blog post, plan, statement, contract draft, story, or similar. Returns a surface_id for subsequent document_update calls. Do NOT write documents to a scratch/temp file or dump them inline in chat — create them here so the user can review, edit, sign/send, and export.

title.description: Initial title for the document (optional, can be updated later)

initial_content.description: Initial Markdown content to populate the editor (optional)

tools.name: document_update
tools.description: Append to or fully replace a document's content. Takes the full Markdown in `content` plus a `mode`: "append" adds it to the end (use this to stream generated content in chunks), "replace" overwrites the entire document. This tool does NOT do targeted edits — for changing specific words, phrases, or sections, use document_replace_text instead. There is no old/new or find/replace parameter here.

surface_id.description: The ID of the document surface to update

content.description: Markdown content to set or append

mode.description: Whether to replace all content or append to the end. Defaults to append.

tools.name: document_read
tools.description: Read the current content of a document by its surface_id when it belongs to the current conversation, or when the current actor is the guardian/local user. Use this to verify document state before making edits.

surface_id.description: The ID of the document to read

tools.name: document_list
tools.description: List documents. Without a query, lists documents in the current conversation. With a query, searches documents by title; guardian/local users can search across conversations, while other actors are scoped to the current conversation.

query.description: Search documents by title. Omit to list only the current conversation's documents.

tools.name: document_delete
tools.description: Delete a document by its surface_id.

surface_id.description: The ID of the document to delete

tools.name: document_find
tools.description: Search for text or a regex pattern within a document. Returns matching lines with line numbers and context — like grep. Use this to locate specific content before making targeted edits with document_replace_text.

query.description: Text or regex pattern to search for

regex.description: Treat query as a regex pattern. Defaults to false (literal match).

tools.name: document_replace_text
tools.description: Find and replace text within a document — like sed. Performs targeted replacements without rewriting the entire document. Supports literal text and regex patterns. Use document_find first to preview what will be matched.

find.description: Text or regex pattern to find

replace.description: Replacement text. When using regex, supports backreferences ($1, $2, etc.).

regex.description: Treat find as a regex pattern. Defaults to false (literal match).

max_replacements.description: Maximum number of replacements to make. Omit to replace all occurrences.

tools.name: comment_list
tools.description: List open comments on a document. Returns all unresolved comments with their content, anchor text, and thread context so you can address user feedback.

tools.name: comment_resolve
tools.description: Mark a comment as resolved after you have addressed the feedback. Use this after editing the document to satisfy the comment.

tools.name: comment_reply
tools.description: Reply to a comment thread. Use this to ask clarifying questions or explain your approach before or after making changes.

comment_id.description: The parent comment ID to reply to

tools.name: document_export_pdf
tools.description: Export an existing document (by surface_id) as a polished PDF delivered as an in-chat attachment the user can download and share. Use when the user asks for a PDF of a document you created, or mentions sending, printing, or sharing it as a file. Finish the document's content first, then export.

surface_id.description: The document's surface id (from document_create or <active_documents>).

tools.name: document_export
tools.description: Export an existing document (by surface_id) as a file in any format, delivered as an in-chat attachment. Pick by what the user will DO with it: "docx" when they or a client will EDIT or redline it in Word (contracts, proposals, anything going through review) — the text stays editable; "pptx" when they will present or edit the document AS SLIDES in PowerPoint — each `#`/`##` becomes a slide, bullets and tables stay editable; "xlsx" to pull the document's tables into a spreadsheet they can re-calculate (pricing, budgets, data); "png" for an image to paste into Slack, a deck or a message (optionally one element via `selector`); "markdown" for the raw source; "html" for a self-contained web page; "pdf" for a fixed, final, printable file (document_export_pdf does the same). IMPORTANT about pptx: it exports STRUCTURE — headings, bullets, tables — as editable 16:9 slides styled by PowerPoint. It is NOT a pixel-faithful copy of a designed layout, and it cannot turn a designed HTML deck built with the app-builder into slides; that deck ships as a PDF via deck_export_pdf. Say which one you produced rather than letting the user believe their designed deck was converted. Finish the document's content first, then export.

surface_id.description: The document's surface id (from document_create or <active_documents>).

format.description: Output format. docx = editable in Word; pptx = editable 16:9 slides built from the headings, bullets and tables (PowerPoint's styling, not a designed layout); xlsx = the document's tables as sheets; png = shareable image; pdf = fixed/printable.

selector.description: PNG only. CSS selector to capture one element (e.g. "table") instead of the whole page.

scale.description: PNG only. Pixel density, 1-4. Default 2 (sharp when shared).

width_px.description: PNG only. Page width in CSS pixels. Default 1000.

tools.name: pdf_create
tools.description: Create a standalone PDF file from full self-contained HTML (or plain markdown) and deliver it as an in-chat attachment. This is the path for every PRESENTED artifact — proposal, one-pager, pitch, brief, client-facing report, case study, quote, invoice, flyer — which must be built with `html` and the skill's house style (references/DESIGNED_PDF.md), never written in the Markdown editor and exported. Use `markdown` only for a plain text file. For prose the user will iterate on, prefer document_create then document_export_pdf. HTML must be self-contained (no external assets — network is blocked during render).

markdown.description: Markdown content (rendered with the document print styling). Provide exactly one of markdown/html.

html.description: Full self-contained HTML (your own styling). Provide exactly one of markdown/html.

tools.name: file_create
tools.description: Create a standalone file — PNG image, HTML page, Markdown, Word .docx, Excel .xlsx or PowerPoint .pptx — from markdown or self-contained HTML, delivered as an in-chat attachment. The non-PDF sibling of pdf_create; use it when the user names a format or says what they'll do with the file: "in Word"/"so I can edit it"/"to redline" → docx (markdown input, stays editable); "in PowerPoint"/"as slides"/"a .pptx they can edit" → pptx (markdown input; each `#`/`##` becomes a slide, bullets and tables stay editable); "as a spreadsheet"/"in Excel" → xlsx (markdown input, one sheet per table); "as an image"/"to paste into Slack or a deck"/"a screenshot of this" → png (html or markdown; `selector` captures one element); a web page or email body → html. HTML input works only for png and html, and must be self-contained (the network is blocked during render). IMPORTANT about pptx: it exports STRUCTURE — headings, bullets, tables — as editable 16:9 slides with PowerPoint's own styling. It is NOT a pixel-faithful copy of a designed layout and it cannot convert a designed HTML deck; a designed deck ships as a PDF (deck_export_pdf in app-builder). Tell the user which one they got. For a PDF use pdf_create.

title.description: Used for the filename, and as the document/workbook title.

format.description: Output format. docx/xlsx/pptx/markdown require `markdown` input; png and html accept either.

markdown.description: Markdown content. Provide exactly one of markdown/html.

html.description: Full self-contained HTML (your own styling), for png or html only. Provide exactly one of markdown/html.

selector.description: PNG only. CSS selector to capture one element (e.g. ".cover") instead of the whole page.

scale.description: PNG only. Pixel density, 1-4. Default 2 (sharp when shared).

width_px.description: PNG only. Page width in CSS pixels. Default 1000.
